To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the presentation of the animation and narration simultaneously, rather than in successive large or small bites, maximized the learning outcomes of the students.
students learn better from animations and narration presented concurrently than when they are presented successively in either small bites or large bites.
Students performed better when the narration was presented concurrently with the animation than when it was presented before or during the animation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of instructional multimedia materials and how they can be used in a way that will maximize learning.

the development of a new approach for the design and development of multimedia communications that are effective in promoting constructivist learning in a way that is consistent with current cognitive theories and research on multimedia learning.
the development of a multimedia learning system that will provide the student with the opportunity to learn about a topic in a way that is most effective for the individual.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

students learn better when they are exposed to multimedia communications with a concurrent presentation of the animation and the narration, compared with the successive presentation of the animation or narration.
the best way of teaching is to use multimedia, and that it should be used in a way that allows learners to construct connections between the words and corresponding pictures.
concurrent presentation of words and pictures is more likely to facilitate the learning of complex material than successive presentation of words and corresponding pictures.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

students who view an animation while listening to an audio narration of the steps depicted in the animation are better able to learn the explanation of the steps in words, to transfer the explanation to new problems, and to match words to corresponding pictures than students who listen to the entire narration before or after viewing the entire animation or who view short portions of the animations while listening to short portions of the narrations.
the concurrent presentation of words and pictures is superior to the successive presentation of words and corresponding pictures for learning.
the concurrent and successive bites groups outperform the successive bites group on retention and transfer.
The main takeaway from our work is that
multimedia presentations that are designed to maximize constructivist learning should present the narration and the pictures at the same time.
we should present multimedia information to learners in a way that minimizes cognitive load.

multimedia presentations can be designed to maximize constructivist learning by presenting the narration and animation at the same time, or at least by presenting the narration before or after the corresponding animation in small bites.
